title: Portability T5a: settings.json paths and interpreter normalization
problem: The in-repo .claude/settings.json has a stale relative path (hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py instead of core/hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py). core/hooks/*.py files resolve the apiary repo root via cwd assumptions rather than $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, which breaks when invoked from other working directories. There is no requirements.txt pinning third-party deps, and the codebase has not been audited for Python 3.14-only syntax — on a fresh clone with Python 3.11, some hooks may not run.
description:
First phase of the portability epic (T5), RE-SCOPED on 2026-04-07 to cover only IN-REPO portability items.

BACKGROUND: The original T5a also included rewriting ~/.claude/settings.json (user-global, outside the repo). That scope item had to be dropped because pipeline/executor.py uses git add/commit to capture step edits and cannot commit files outside the repo working tree. The first pipeline run of T5a failed at step 1 on exactly this issue (see scribe blocker #203). The ~/.claude/settings.json rewrite is now tracked as scribe TODO #205 and will be hand-edited out-of-band when the user is awake.

KEY RESOLVED QUESTION: Claude Code DOES expand $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR as a real environment variable in hook subprocess environments (confirmed 2026-04-07 against the Claude Code hooks guide). Hook commands can reference 'python $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/core/hooks/foo.py' directly with no wrapper layer. POSIX-shell syntax only; cmd.exe would need %VAR% — apiary runs on Windows-bash, macOS, and Linux bash/zsh, so assume POSIX. Standardize on bash-style expansion and document the assumption.

Scope of work (IN-REPO ONLY):

1. Fix stale relative path in .claude/settings.json (in-repo):
   - Current hook entry points at 'python hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py' but the script lives at core/hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py.
   - Rewrite the command to use '$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR' + the correct relative path: 'python $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/core/hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py'.
   - Verify the hook still fires by exercising a repo CLI tool that enforce_cli_lookup guards (e.g. scribe/notes.py).

2. Audit core/hooks/*.py for cwd-based apiary-location assumptions:
   - Identify every place that resolves the apiary repo root by reading cwd or assuming a specific directory layout.
   - Replace with os.environ.get('CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR') and a Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N] fallback when the env var is unset (for portability when hooks are invoked outside a Claude Code session, e.g. during tests).
   - Do NOT touch subprocess or null-device code (that's T5b's scope).

3. Add requirements.txt at repo root:
   - List all third-party Python deps imported anywhere in the repo (grep for 'import ' in core/hooks/, pipeline/, scribe/, harden/, budgeter/, scripts/).
   - Pin each dep to a version RANGE (e.g. 'foo>=1.2,<2.0'), not exact pins.
   - Stdlib modules are excluded by definition.

4. Pick a minimum Python version and document it:
   - Recommendation: 3.11 (widely available, avoids 3.14-only syntax).
   - Audit the repo for 3.14-only syntax (e.g. t-strings, PEP 695 type aliases with newer forms, etc.) and back-port anything found.
   - Document the minimum version in README.md or CLAUDE.md (a 'Requirements' section near the top).

Definition of done:
- .claude/settings.json (in-repo) hook command uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR + core/hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py, and the hook fires correctly.
- core/hooks/*.py resolve the repo root via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR + pathlib fallback, not cwd.
- requirements.txt exists at repo root with all third-party deps pinned to ranges.
- Minimum Python version is declared in README.md or CLAUDE.md, and the codebase is free of syntax that only works on 3.14+.
- No regression: existing hooks still fire, existing pipeline still runs.

Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE:
- ~/.claude/settings.json rewrite (user-global, outside repo — will be hand-edited, see scribe TODO #205).
- Subprocess / null-device / pathlib audit (that is T5b).
- Bootstrap script, stable project key, state migration (that is T5c).
- PORTABILITY.md and fresh-VM acceptance test (that is T5d).
scope: .claude/settings.json (in-repo only — NOT the user-global ~/.claude/settings.json), core/hooks/*.py (apiary repo-root resolution only, no subprocess/null-device changes), requirements.txt (new), README.md or CLAUDE.md (Requirements section with minimum Python version). Strictly no subprocess rewrites, no bootstrap, no docs beyond the min-Python note.
context: Phase 1 of the portability epic split, re-scoped after the out-of-repo scoping bug (scribe blocker #203). T5b (shell hygiene), T5c (bootstrap + stable project key), and T5d (docs + fresh-VM validation) are queued in backlog/ and will be picked up by the detached overnight cron in mtime order after each prior phase's pipeline/* branch is merged. The user-global ~/.claude/settings.json rewrite is tracked separately as scribe TODO #205 and will be done by hand when the user is awake (a broken hook would brick the session, so it can't be done unattended).
